title: Remotes, Fetch, Pull & Push Collaboration
description: Connect local repositories to remote hosts like GitHub, understand remote-tracking branches, and synchronize changes with fetch, pull, and push.

blocks.content: Your teammate has new commits on the shared project. You need to bring that history into your local copy deliberately. What is the smallest Git action that keeps the work safe?

A remote is another copy of a repository, often shared by a team. `git fetch` downloads new history without changing your files; `git pull` fetches and integrates it.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Working files"] -->|"choose an action"| B["Git history"] -->|"share or recover"| C["Team project"]
```

blocks.question: What is the difference between fetch and pull?
options: Fetch downloads history; pull also integrates it
Fetch deletes history; pull creates it
blocks.explanation: Fetch lets you inspect new remote history before changing your working branch.

blocks.prompt: Model the Git idea in a tiny simulator. Export a function named `fetchFile` that takes `(working, staged, file)` and returns a new staged list containing `file` once. Do not change either input list.

tests.description: works when no working files are listed yet
